messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: streaming tail-latency p99 spike detected in eu-west2 (service: streaming-gen). Paging on-call.
maria: on it. seeing p95 ~300ms -> p99 ~2.1s for streaming gateway. Streaming stalls reported by customers. Links: https://telemetry.redwood/streams/eu-west2/526789
ashish: I'm seeing elevated retransmit counts on the vpc-egress paths between az-b and az-c for that cluster. NAT ephemeral exhaustion-ish pattern in the socket table.
jessie: runtime telemetry shows KV-cache miss rate steady, so this looks like network stalls not model runtime. tcp handshake/syn retransmit counts spiking.
maria: can we confirm DNS resolution or TLS handshake spikes? those tend to surface similarly.
ashish: DNS lookups look fine. TLS handshake RTT histogram moved from 50-100ms -> a long tail 800ms-2s. Packet loss on egress path ~0.6% (normally <0.05%).
kevin: customer-impact calc: ~4.2% of streaming sessions saw at least one stall >1s in the last 12m. flagging as customer-impacting.
maria: triggering live mitigation playbook: eu-west2 egress reroute -> fallback to alternative NAT path. executing now.
ashish: running quick probe:```sh
# netstat snapshot on gw-12
Tcp: RcvQ=0, SendQ=0, Rto=1200ms, retransmits=178
established=3120, timewait=743
``` 
ashish: also bumping SNAT port pool on the egress nodes to buy breathing room.
jessie: can we TTL-stop streaming to affected route and serve via warm fallback cluster (eu-west1) for critical customers? that's heavier cost but reduces user impact.
maria: starting selective reroute for high-traffic prefixes -> apply route-policy `egress-priority` now.
kevin: pinging support to proactively message customers on impacted plans; include mitigation ETA ~15m.
ashish: applied iptables tweak to increase ephemeral port range, and issued a config to reduce TCP syn retries from 6 -> 4 for faster failure detection. monitoring.
maria: quick check of the stream logs after reroute: p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 480ms within 4m. p95 back to ~320ms.
jessie: runtime note: streaming tail stalls due to retransmit queueing at the NAT hop. once reroute was active we saw fewer stalls and less kernel-level retransmit.
maria: handoff: oncall-2 take over for next 60m. I will leave the runbook notes below and handoff checklist.
oncall-2: ack. I see health panels are greening. I'll keep the reroute in place and watch for regression for the next hour.
maria: runbook notes: - root cause likely intermittent cross-zone egress path packet loss causing TLS handshake tail and retransmits. - mitigation performed: selective egress reroute + SNAT port expansion + syn-retries tuning. - customer impact estimate: 4.2% sessions saw stalls, major customers affected: cust-45, cust-78 (streaming quality degradations). - follow-ups: validate routing policy propagation with cloud provider, schedule deep pcap capture window, consider permanent multipath routing to avoid single egress hop.
ashish: follow-up action item: open infra ticket INFRA-9482 to coordinate with cloud on egress fabric repairs and request dump of egress switch counters between az-b/az-c.
jessie: suggest adding additional runtime backoff for streaming handshake to avoid retry storms at client side; filing RUNTIME-222.
kevin: i'll draft customer comms with the quantified impact and mitigation timeline.
oncall-2: taking ownership. will escalate to paging if p99 climbs above 1s again. closing my notification, will update thread with any changes. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks everyone. leaving postmortem TODOs in the incident tracker and marking as SLO-breach-possible.
